plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when my value exceeds the price) and never miss profitable opportunities (I win whenever it's profitable to do so). Therefore, the optimal bid is simply my value of $13.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy since payment depends on the second-highest bid, not my own bid. Bidding truthfully ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the competition, and pay less than my value, maximizing expected profit regardless of others' strategies. With a value of $15, I should bid exactly $15 to align my bid with my true valuation, avoiding overbidding (risk of negative profit) or underbidding (missing profitable wins).

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy: you win precisely when your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're the winner). Bidding higher risks overpaying if you win, and bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. Since this holds regardless of others' strategies, the optimal action is straightforward: bid exactly my private value of $47.
